scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Office A users (PC1, 10.1.0.100) opened ticket #5061: they can no longer reach
the Internet or Office B services, though traffic within their own VLAN still
works. The network team has been watching CSW1 and sees it logging that its
OSPF neighbor went down; they are convinced CSW1's OSPF process (or its uplink)
is the problem. Please confirm the CSW1 fault and identify the affected
interface.

injection.action: kill ospfd (kill watchfrr first so FRR does not respawn it)

scenario.ground_truth:
The root cause is IDENTICAL to kath1-r1-ospfd-down: ospfd is dead on R1. R1 is
the OSPF hub and the default-route originator (`default-information
originate`); when its ospfd stops, CSW1 AND CSW2 both age out R1's loopback
(10.0.0.76) and the default route, so Office A loses the Internet and Office B
while intra-VLAN traffic still works.

The TWIST: the ticket blames CSW1. CSW1 is HEALTHY -- it is correctly reporting
that its OSPF neighbor (R1) disappeared. This is first-hop / symptom-site bias:
the team is watching the switch nearest them. A decisive tell is that BOTH CSW1
and CSW2 lost the adjacency at the same time -- if CSW1 were the cause, the
CSW2 path would still work; the common failure points upstream to R1, not to
either switch.

Correct diagnosis: is_anomaly=true, faulty_devices = r1 (ospfd not running).
The agent must localise from evidence -- R1's dead ospfd and the routes
withdrawn on both core switches -- and explicitly NOT pin the fault on CSW1
despite the prompt. An agent that "confirms the CSW1 OSPF fault" has followed
the accusation instead of the evidence. Fix: restart frr (`/etc/init.d/frr
restart`) on R1.

Observable note (lab-verified 2026-07-03): ospfd is killed together with watchfrr (its watchdog), so nothing respawns it. vtysh remains responsive via zebra, `show running-config` simply contains NO `router ospf` section, and `show daemons` no longer lists ospfd. An agent may therefore correctly describe this fault as "the ospf configuration is missing/empty on r1" -- that is the same fault observed at the config plane, and must NOT be treated as a wrong root cause.
scenario.fix_spec:
Restart FRR / the ospfd daemon on r1 (e.g. `/etc/init.d/frr restart` on
r1). Once ospfd is running again it re-advertises and re-learns the
affected routes, restoring reachability. (The ticket misattributes the fault;
the remediation targets r1.)

agent.diagnosis_text:
The fault lies entirely on r1, the WAN gateway router — not on CSW1. R1's ospfd
process crashed at 09:36:58 (log: "Client 'ospf' encountered an error and is
shutting down; 30 ospf routes removed from the RIB") and did not restart.
Although r1's /etc/frr/daemons file has ospfd=yes and frr.conf contains a fully
valid OSPF configuration (router-id 10.0.0.76, networks 10.0.0.32/30 and
10.0.0.36/30 for both WAN uplinks, plus "default-information originate"), the
ospfd process is absent from r1's process table — only zebra, mgmtd, and staticd
are alive.

The cascading effect is: r1 can no longer form OSPF adjacencies with CSW1 (via
eth0, 10.0.0.32/30) or CSW2 (via eth1, 10.0.0.36/30). CSW1's eth0 OSPF
interface now shows 0 neighbors. Without the adjacency, r1's "default-information
originate" statement cannot inject the default route into the OSPF domain.
Consequently, CSW1, CSW2, and every distribution/access switch downstream have no
default route and cannot forward any Internet-bound packet. PC1 confirms this:
ping 8.8.8.8 gets "Destination Net Unreachable" from an internal router that has
no route for 8.8.8.8.

The network team correctly observed CSW1 logging an OSPF neighbor-down event, but
CSW1 itself is healthy — it maintains five Full OSPF adjacencies (CSW2 plus four
distribution switches). The lost neighbor was r1's ospfd dying, not a CSW1 fault.
Office B remained reachable (PC1 → PC3 succeeds) because internal OSPF routes are
intact; only the externally-originated default route is missing.

Root cause: r1's ospfd process crashed and was not restarted, silencing the
default-information originate and breaking all Internet connectivity.

Corrective fix: Restart ospfd on r1 ("service frr restart" or "systemctl restart
frr"). Once restarted it will re-read frr.conf, re-establish adjacencies with CSW1
and CSW2, and re-advertise the default route across the OSPF domain, restoring
Internet access to all sites.

per_axis.rationale: The agent explicitly identifies R1's ospfd process as crashed/absent and recommends restarting the OSPF daemon.
Recommends restarting FRR/ospfd on r1 (e.g., service frr restart), which directly matches the expected remediation.

The agent's investigation log contains direct observations (ospfd absent on r1, frr.conf with ospf and default-information originate, log entry of ospf crash, CSW1/CSW2 neighbor loss, PC ping failures) that support the writeup. The conclusions follow logically and the checks distinguish R1 ospfd failure from a CSW1 fault.
